MetodologIA · Class 01 · Practice workbook

Turn one of your questions into learning you can repeat.

Opening a tool without a clear question and sources usually produces answers that are hard to judge.

Journey outcomeA purposeful source base, reviewed evidence, a sufficiency verdict and an AI role chosen with judgment.
View promptsView masterclass

The workbook orders preparation, practice and consolidation so you do not depend on one conversation.

Define the topic, load relevant sources, run one instruction and record how your understanding changed.

Keep citations, decisions, open doubts and a result you can rebuild without copying the answer.

00 · How to use it

How to use it

Start by preparing a real case. In class you complete five guided steps. Then you can deepen the work, consolidate evidence and, optionally, turn reviewed research into a skill.

Usage conditions

Each provider can change its terms, limits, pricing and features. The essential practice does not require a paid subscription. For sheets 2 and 3, a paid ChatGPT or Claude plan may provide more continuity and capacity, but it does not guarantee better results. Always verify current official conditions.

Preparation · one input, three moves

Prepare your case

Start with free-form dictation. Reuse the same field as a handoff space: after prompt 1 paste the confirmed version; after prompt 2 paste the agreed brief; then run the preplan. Nothing is retained after reload.

01

Dump, clean and confirm

Prompt 01
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

I want to dump and order my dictation before the workshop. I am after [SESSION PURPOSE] and I ask for a [CLEANING LEVEL], conservative or aggressive. I paste my dictation here: {{BRAIN_DUMP}}. Work only with that dictation and with attachments you actually received: do not invent sentences, data or attachments I never dictated. Strip repetition at the requested [CLEANING LEVEL] without erasing intent or nuance; if cleaning threatens a technical term I used, keep my term and tell me. If [SESSION PURPOSE] arrives empty, ask me for it before cleaning; if the dictation is unintelligible, ask me to record it again. Order purpose, context, ideas, questions, constraints, mentioned sources and pending decisions by their distance to [SESSION PURPOSE]. Separate what I said, what you interpreted and what stayed empty. Confirm the understanding in five points at most and declare whatever you could not interpret instead of filling it in. Then ask me at most three strategic questions, one per turn and waiting for my answer: first the one that can change the purpose, then the one that challenges an assumption, then the one that opens value. Close with the clean version and what changed in the understanding. If the dictation already arrives clean, say so and return only the gaps. If I ask you for a solution or a tool, declare it out of this turn.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every technical term of the dictation appears unchanged in the clean version, with no paraphrase
  • The confirmation holds five points or fewer and each one can be marked right or corrected
  • Questions arrive one at a time: the next appears only after the previous answer

Edge cases

  • Unintelligible dictation: a new recording is requested instead of filling the gap
  • Missing session purpose: it is requested before cleaning, because the ordering depends on it

Trade-offs

  • Fidelity to the voice in exchange for less polished prose
  • This turn does not separate authorship because it assumes a single voice; in exchange it exposes the cleaning-level control that the team cell pins to conservative
  • The original definition of done promised that the person "discovers possibilities": it is replaced by facts of the turn — points confirmed, terms preserved, questions answered — because discovery is neither produced nor verified by the prompt

Assumptions

  • The dictation is the only available material: there are no implicit attachments

Limits

  • It confirms understanding; it neither classifies the intent nor writes the assignment
  • It proposes no material and designs no Notebook, and it does not promise the understanding is right: it only makes it reviewable
02

Define the learning assignment

Prompt 02
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

I want to turn my confirmed understanding into an assignment before talking about tools. My target outcome is [OUTCOME] and I will use it for [DECISION OR USE]. I paste the material here: {{BRAIN_DUMP}}. Classify my main intent among study, learn, create, decide, prepare a conversation, configure an advisor or configure a coach; if [OUTCOME] and [DECISION OR USE] point at two intents, declare as main the one that blocks the other and secondary the remaining one; if none fits, say so and propose the closest. Write the sentence "I want to understand or produce [OUTCOME] so I can [DECISION OR USE]". Define my audience, deadline, current level and constraints from what I dictated; whatever is unsaid, ask me for it: do not invent sources, deadlines or constraints. Set one minimum observable evidence: something I can show that another person can call done or not done without knowing my intent. State what is out of scope and which decision stays mine. Return a one-page brief with those sections in that order and ask me for confirmation section by section, marking each one as confirmed or corrected. If the material arrives with no clean version, confirm the understanding in five points first. If I ask to jump to tools, declare it out: the assignment comes first.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The brief carries the nine sections in the requested order and no section is left empty without saying why
  • The minimum evidence can be called done or not done by someone who does not know the intent
  • Every section comes back marked as confirmed or corrected, not approved in bulk

Edge cases

  • Mixed intent: the blocking one is declared main, with the secondary one placed after it
  • Constraint or deadline never dictated: it is requested instead of completed

Trade-offs

  • One more step before touching tools in exchange for not building the wrong Notebook
  • This turn asks for evidence tailored to me and does not require comparability across people, which is what the team cell adds along with the deciding role
  • The original definition of done promised the assignment "enables a later decision about the needed Notebook and sources": that happens in a later turn, so what is checked here is what this turn does produce — confirmed sections and declarable evidence

Assumptions

  • The understanding arrives already confirmed; if not, the prompt itself runs a minimal confirmation before classifying
  • The final decision is human in every case

Limits

  • It produces the assignment; it neither picks a tool nor selects material
  • It does not guarantee the assignment is the right one: it makes it explicit so I can confirm or correct it
03

Turn it into a NotebookLM preplan

Prompt 03
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

I want a NotebookLM preplan before the workshop. My confirmed assignment is [CONFIRMED ASSIGNMENT] and my candidate material is [AVAILABLE MATERIAL]. I paste it here: {{BRAIN_DUMP}}. Classify the case among study, learn something new, create source-grounded content, prepare a decision or meeting, configure an advisor, configure a coach, or turn research into a skill; if none fits, say so and propose the closest. Write "This Notebook exists to…" derived from [CONFIRMED ASSIGNMENT], and define my audience, the observable outcome and the final decision, which stays mine. Split [AVAILABLE MATERIAL] into three lists: loadable, gaps to research, and excluded by privacy or rights, each exclusion with its reason. If everything ends up excluded, stop and declare coverage_gap instead of quietly degrading the plan. If the material exceeds the scope of [CONFIRMED ASSIGNMENT], the assignment wins and the rest is set aside; if [CONFIRMED ASSIGNMENT] arrives empty, confirm it with me in five points before preplanning. Recommend a source-grounded role —teacher, advisor or coach— and its explicit boundary. Deliver the plan mapped to the five workshop steps: build, audit, research, decide sufficiency and activate the role. Close with the first evidence I should produce. Do not invent sources, attachments or NotebookLM capabilities.

Level 2Structured

Makes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every candidate item appears in exactly one of the three lists, and every excluded one carries its reason
  • The recommended role comes with a boundary sentence saying what it will not do
  • The five workshop steps are named, not cited as an external reference

Edge cases

  • Empty assignment: it is confirmed in five points before preplanning instead of being inferred
  • Zero loadable material: the preplan stops with coverage_gap declared

Trade-offs

  • A conservative preplan in exchange for a clean start with nothing that has to be pulled back later
  • This turn excludes material by privacy or rights case by case on my own judgement; the team cell treats exclusion as policy and adds an external reviewer
  • The original definition of done said the preplan "lets the person open NotebookLM and begin": that happens outside the turn, so what is checked here are the pieces the preplan does deliver

Assumptions

  • The assignment arrives confirmed from an earlier turn; if not, the prompt itself confirms it before preplanning
  • The candidate material is what the person names: there are no implicit attachments

Limits

  • It preplans; it neither creates the Notebook, uploads material, nor runs the workshop steps
  • It promises no tool capability beyond what is documented, and no accuracy of the answers

Before you continue

Prepare for the workshop

01

Prerequisites

  • Google account with access to NotebookLM.
  • Updated desktop browser; phone as a secondary device.
  • Basic familiarity with AI chat: write, iterate and review.
  • Willingness to learn a new way of working.
02

Inputs

  • A real topic, decision or problem.
  • Three to eight sources you are allowed to use.
  • The audience and outcome you want to produce.
  • A criterion for deciding when the base is sufficient.
03

Working boundaries

  • Do not upload personal, confidential or restricted data.
  • Citations support review; they do not guarantee accuracy.
  • The workbook does not save or send answers.
  • The final decision and risk remain human.

W00 · Total duration 60–120 min · Requirement: Google account, browser and real topic. Privacy: do not upload personal or confidential data. This document does not save or send your answers; print or save locally only if you choose. You decide; NotebookLM organizes and cites; the facilitator guides.
NotebookLM can answer from selected sources and show citations; these aids do not guarantee accuracy. Inspect the source and keep human judgment. Deep Research requires users to be 18 or older and availability can vary by account, plan and surface; check official help.

01–03 · Workbook

Three practice routes.

01 · In session

Five steps

Define purpose, review sources and decide when evidence is sufficient.

1

A first base with a purpose

Expected evidence: a decision and cited evidence.

Inputs: topic, purpose and context · Action: run and review · Output: cited response · Check: inspect the source · Next: decide whether to continue.

Prompt 1
1Level 1 · DirectA clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.
Level 1Direct

A clear instruction, ready to discuss and refine.

Step 1 of the workshop: I want a useful, verifiable knowledge base about [TOPIC] and nothing is loaded yet. I need it for [DECISION OR RESULT]; my context is [CONTEXT] and my audience is [AUDIENCE]. Define scope and questions; explain the essentials and what changed since [CUTOFF DATE]; prioritize primary sources; include tensions and evidence limits; separate facts, interpretations and uncertainty, tagging every uncertain line as "uncertain: X is missing"; recommend each source with title, author, date, link and reason. Do not stop at scoping and do not close on a sufficiency rule: deliver a cited report I can import as my first source and audit in the next step. If no primary sources are reachable, deliver the shorter report and list the gaps instead of filling them. Do not invent sources, citations or dates, and do not present more certainty than the sources support.
2Level 2 · StructuredMakes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.
Level 2Structured

Makes inputs, options, flow and expected result explicit.

# systemStep 1 facilitator: produces the first source of the workshop# Guardrails- Never invent sources, citations or dates- No reachable primary sources: shorter report with gaps listed, never filled- Do not close on a sufficiency rule: this step delivers a report, not a verdict# Definition of DoneImportable report: scope, essentials, tensions and sources present, every source carrying its five fields and every uncertain line tagged.# user# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.# TaskTurn a topic with no loaded base into an importable cited report that chains into the audit step# Workflow1. Record topic, decision, context, audience and cutoff date2. Define the scope and frame the essential questions3. Explain the essentials and what changed since the cutoff date4. Prioritize primary sources with title, author, date, link and reason5. Separate facts, interpretations and uncertainty and tag every uncertain line6. Deliver the cited report ready to import and audit in the next step# Expected output- Cited report with scope, essentials, tensions and limits- Primary sources with title, author, date, link and reason- List of open gaps and of the lines tagged as uncertain
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The report carries the four fixed sections: scope, essentials, tensions and recommended sources
  • Every recommended source carries title, author, date, link and reason; without the five fields it stays out
  • Every uncertain line carries the tag "uncertain: X is missing"; untagged lines read as asserted

Edge cases

  • No reachable primary sources: the report ships shorter and the gaps stay listed for the research brief
  • No decision or result declared: the prompt asks before scoping

Trade-offs

  • An imperfect first report in exchange for opening the cycle with material of my own that can be audited
  • A fixed cutoff leaves later publications out, in exchange for making "recent changes" checkable

Assumptions

  • The report will be imported into the Notebook as the first source and audited in the next step
  • The anatomy of scoping, splitting facts from interpretations and prioritizing primary sources with a reason is inherited from the standalone variant 01; here it ends in a cited report, not in a sufficiency rule
  • If prior preparation happened, the preplan orients the scope; it brings no loaded sources: the Notebook is still empty when step 1 starts

Limits

  • It produces the first base, not a sufficient base: sufficiency is decided when the cycle closes
  • It does not audit or rank the gaps of what it delivers: that belongs to W02

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The summary fits in eight lines and the table carries all five columns
  • Every finding carries the citation of the selected source that holds it
  • "What I can claim today" is a list where every line carries its citation: without one the line stays out, and that rule replaces the adjective "honest"

Edge cases

  • Single-source base: the prompt forces a bias audit before any other dimension
  • Findings that contradict across sources: they are typed as a tension in the table instead of averaged

Trade-offs

  • A fixed format in exchange for comparability across workshop iterations
  • Deferring the sufficiency verdict frustrates whoever wants an answer today, in exchange for not closing before the missing material is imported

Assumptions

  • The base was built in step 1 and is already imported into the Notebook
  • The core dimensions (coverage, freshness, bias, redundancy) are inherited from the standalone audit 05; here they do not close in a verdict

Limits

  • It does not write the assistant instruction or its starter prompts
  • It does not decide sufficiency: that belongs to W04, and the research brief to W03

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The brief carries objective, in and out of scope, minimum evidence and acceptance criteria: it is reviewed as a checklist, not by impression
  • Every acceptance criterion can be checked one by one against the answer received
  • The chosen gap is justified against the declared result: the winner is the one blocking most claimable lines

Edge cases

  • No prior diagnosis: the prompt asks to run the audit instead of inventing gaps
  • Two gaps tied on impact: it asks instead of deciding for the user

Trade-offs

  • One gap per iteration in exchange for scope control across the cycle
  • Writing the brief instead of answering it adds a manual step in exchange for the answer entering the Notebook as a citable source

Assumptions

  • A diagnosis from the prior step exists with prioritized gaps
  • The brief anatomy — in and out of scope, tensions, minimum evidence, acceptance — is inherited from the standalone research 03; there the research runs, here it is only commissioned
  • Deep Research is available for the account: availability varies by plan and age, and the prompt does not promise it

Limits

  • It generates the brief, it does not run the research or guarantee the answer closes the gap
  • It does not re-audit the base or decide sufficiency: that belongs to W02 and W04

# systemStep 4 judge: weighs the delta and closes or repeats the cycle# Guardrails- Never invent closures, confirmations or sources- Do not verify claim by claim: this step measures the delta- A new source contradicting the base: no sufficient verdict without resolving the tension# Definition of DoneVerdict never alone: the point-by-point comparison complete, the residual risk written, and sufficient with limits or repeat with the next prompt.# user# InputsComplete or adjust values in brackets before running.# TaskCompare the base after the import against the previous audit and issue a sufficiency verdict with limits# Workflow1. Record the purpose and the gap audited in the previous round2. Compare the current base against the previous audit point by point3. Mark claims confirmed or refuted and any new tensions4. Score the value of every imported source on the declared scale5. Issue sufficient with limits or repeat with the next prompt, and write down the residual risk# Expected output- Point-by-point comparison against the previous audit- Value of each source on the declared scale and the residual risk- Sufficient verdict with limits, or repeat with the next prompt
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The comparison walks the four points of the previous audit: gap, claims, tensions and residual risk
  • The verdict never travels alone: sufficient carries its limits and repeat carries the next prompt
  • Sufficient has an operational definition — no open gap blocks the declared purpose — checkable against the gap list

Edge cases

  • New sources that contradict the base: the verdict cannot be sufficient without resolving the tension
  • A cycle past three rounds: the prompt recommends re-scoping instead of leaving the loop open

Trade-offs

  • Stopping on sufficient evidence in exchange for incomplete coverage, declared in the verdict limits
  • The base text advice "do not seek perfection" is replaced by the checkable condition "no open gap blocks the purpose": the tone is lost and a verifiable test is gained; no other step 4 instruction is lost

Assumptions

  • A previous audit from step 2 exists and new sources were imported into the Notebook
  • The core "claims confirmed or refuted" is inherited from the standalone cross-check 04, which weighs one claim at a time, and the sufficiency verdict from the standalone audit 05; here both apply to the delta of the base

Limits

  • It decides sufficiency over the set, it does not verify each claim in depth: that belongs to 04
  • It does not activate the conversational role over the closed base: that belongs to W05

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The three roles behave differently and the difference shows in the first turn: explaining, recommending with risk, or making the user rephrase
  • Every turn carries a citation from the base or an explicit statement of limit: no turn without one of the two
  • Every claim is tagged as cited evidence, inference or missing data

Edge cases

  • Question outside the base: the role states it and proposes a brief instead of answering unsupported
  • Request for certainty the base does not hold: the available evidence and the remaining gap are shown

Trade-offs

  • A role bounded to the base in exchange for reliability: the role knows less than it would unbounded, and says so
  • A light activation instead of the full teaching cycle: learning depth is lost and a role usable in one turn is gained

Assumptions

  • The base was declared sufficient in the previous step and the role works only on it
  • The mother rule of citing and splitting evidence, inference and missing data is inherited from the standalone coach 02; there the teaching flow is complete, here the activation is light

Limits

  • It activates a conversational role; it does not grade level or give scores: that belongs to W08
  • It does not design the persistent instruction or the Notebook starter prompts: that belongs to W10

02 · Deepening

Guided practice

Prompts 6–10 to create, apply, assess and rehearse from the sources.

Source rubric: coverage · authority · freshness · diversity · citations · sufficiency.

Insufficient: evidence is missing or weak sources dominate.

In progress: partial coverage and reviewable citations.

Sufficient: coverage, authority, freshness, diversity, citations and residual risk are explicit.

Write citing every material claim and labelling as inference whatever the base does not support5. Close with the final piece, its sources and three typed editorial decisions with their reason# Expected output- Final piece with thesis, tension and limit- List of sources cited per material claim, with inferences labelled- Three typed editorial decisions (left out, simplified, highlighted) with their reason
Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The piece carries one single thesis and every material claim is cited from the base
  • Anything not cited is labelled inference, so a reviewer can count them
  • The three editorial decisions are typed as left out, simplified or highlighted, with a reason: they are not adjectives

Edge cases

  • Base without evidence for the requested thesis: a sustainable thesis is proposed instead of forcing it
  • No declared length: it is requested before writing

Trade-offs

  • A less striking piece in exchange for traceability: every material claim stays tied to the base
  • The workshop metadata (when, inputs, output, limit, example) is preserved whole: when becomes the when field, the example becomes example, the output becomes evidence, the no-external-facts limit becomes a guardrail and the inputs become the variables

Assumptions

  • The base arrives audited and declared sufficient in earlier workshop steps; W06 does not judge it again

Limits

  • It creates the piece; it does not publish it: RENDERED_DRAFT is not published and the channel is decided elsewhere
  • It neither ranks a catalogue of use cases (W07) nor rehearses the spoken defence (W09)

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Both scales are declared before scoring: value 1-5 by effect on the role and effort 1-5 by hours and complexity
  • Every ranked case carries cited support from the base; those without it appear marked speculative
  • The seven-day experiment declares an observable metric and its threshold

Edge cases

  • Base without domain material: fewer than ten cases come out and the gap is declared instead of filled
  • Tied score: the lower effort tiebreak applies

Trade-offs

  • Fewer and more defensible cases: demanding cited support shrinks the catalogue in exchange for surviving review
  • The workshop metadata is preserved whole: the when becomes the when field, the pilot example becomes example, the ten ranked cases become evidence, the do-not-invent-ROI limit becomes a guardrail and the role and context inputs become the variables

Assumptions

  • The base arrives audited; a person ranks and decides the pilot, not the recommendation

Limits

  • It estimates neither ROI nor prices, and does not replace the judgement of whoever decides
  • It ranks where to apply the base; it neither drafts the piece (W06) nor writes the final assistant instruction (W10)

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Every answer gets one of the three rubric grades and the quote that justifies it
  • Level advance only happens on demonstrated, so the final level is a condition, not an impression
  • The close delivers strengths, gaps, sources to revisit and one practice, not a performance adjective

Edge cases

  • Foundations not demonstrated: the level repeats instead of advancing
  • Question without coverage: it is replaced and declared

Trade-offs

  • Less depth than the reusable assessor in exchange for a short workshop session tied to the Notebook
  • Receipt for the reframed token: the frozen text asked to «explain»; here it is preserved as a quoted correction of the missing fragment, not as teaching, so the coach mechanism is not invaded; nothing else from the frozen text is dropped

Assumptions

  • The sources are the workshop Notebook and the instrument runs inside the session

Limits

  • It measures inside the workshop; the reusable instrument with its own rubric is 08
  • It neither teaches nor accompanies understanding: that is the coach activation W05
  • Accuracy is not guaranteed: the level measures correspondence with the source, not truth of the source

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • The opening fixes audience, outcome and time before the first question
  • The level rises only if the previous answer quoted the base and answered: escalation is a condition, not a mood
  • The three improvements each name an action and a quote from the base

Edge cases

  • No piece to defend: it stops instead of simulating over nothing
  • Little time: questions drop, demand does not

Trade-offs

  • A lighter simulation than the autonomous version in exchange for a workshop session that asks for context instead of demanding fixed variables
  • The workshop metadata is preserved whole: the when becomes the when field, the hostile QBR becomes example, rehearsal and improvements become evidence, the do-not-simulate-certainty limit becomes a guardrail and the audience, outcome and time inputs become the asked opening

Assumptions

  • The workshop Notebook is active as the evidence base and the piece to defend already exists

Limits

  • It tests the argument; it neither drafts nor restructures it: producing is W06
  • It is the guided workshop form; the autonomous rehearsal with fixed variables is 09
  • It measures the defence, not the truth of the content: surviving pressure does not validate the thesis

Return only the final result and closing metadata.### Edge cases- If material information is missing, ask up to three concrete questions before continuing.- If sources conflict, surface the tension and do not force a conclusion.- If evidence is insufficient, declare coverage_gap and state what would close it.## C — CriterionOutput:- Personalized instruction with role, tasks, limits, citations and quality criterion- Exactly 10 starter prompts without overlap between them- Five-line test guide with one out-of-base question and facts, inferences and missing data separatedObservable acceptance criteria:- The result answers the purpose and respects the declared scope.- Every material claim links to a source or is marked as inference, assumption, or gap.- Boundaries, confidence, and the next verifiable step are explicit.Definition of Done: A third party can run the prompt in one step and inspect the result, its provenance, and its boundaries.## Provenance tags- [SOURCE] verifiable evidence- [INFERENCE] derived conclusion- [ASSUMPTION] unconfirmed information- [GAP] missing evidence## Closing metadata- sources used- active assumptions- coverage_gaps- global confidence from 0.0 to 1.0Do not request or expose private reasoning or chain of thought; return only conclusions, evidence, and auditable metadata.

Why it works

Acceptance criteria

  • Exactly 10 starter prompts, none repeating what another covers
  • The test guide includes an out-of-base question that passes only if the assistant declares the limit
  • The instruction declares limits and a citation rule coherent with the sufficiency verdict already issued, not a new one

Edge cases

  • Constraints clashing with the purpose: it stops before writing the instruction
  • Private material: the non-exposure limit is written

Trade-offs

  • A conservative configuration in exchange for less apparent reach: the assistant promises what the base supports
  • The workshop metadata is preserved whole: the when becomes the when field, the source-grounded coach becomes example, the configuration with 10 starters becomes evidence, the do-not-invent-capabilities limit becomes a guardrail and the purpose, user and limits inputs become the variables; the non-exposure limit for private material lives in guardrails and edge cases because the prompt budget cannot hold all three conditions at once

Assumptions

  • The base arrives audited and declared sufficient in earlier steps; the audit configuration is input, not the final instruction

Limits

  • It configures the assistant; it neither re-audits sources nor issues a sufficiency verdict: that closed in earlier workshop steps; from 07 the recommended configuration arrives, not the final instruction
  • It does not rank which cases are worth covering: that is W07
  • It authorizes neither publication nor connectors: RENDERED_DRAFT is not published

P10 gate: purpose, two decisive sources, one accepted gap and a BASE SUFFICIENT or REPEAT RESEARCH verdict.

03 · Consolidation

Transfer and decide

Consolidate with evidence and your own explanation.

Independent challenge

Create a Notebook for a real decision, run steps 1–5 and use one deepening prompt. Deliver a source map, a sufficiency verdict and a three-minute explanation.

Teach-back: explain the method in 3 minutes. Second context: repeat it for another decision. Continuity: schedule a review in 7 days.

Complete

Complete: reviewable evidence exists.

Pending

Pending: the next action is clear.

coverage_gap

coverage_gap: a source, context or test is missing.

05 · Learn · Apprehend · Evolve

Choose your route

Estimated times. They vary with your iterations.

01≈ 30 min

Essential practice

Five steps to learn how to learn and configure your Notebook.

021–2 h

10-step route

Deepen, create, assess, simulate and configure through iterations.

032–4 h

Extended route

Turn reviewed research into a skill and test a local MCP connection.

01

Useful assistants

In 2026 assistants coexist with more autonomous agents. They remain useful for a clear function, stable instructions, fast creation, and controllable token use. They do not replace judgment or turn weak sources into evidence.

02

Reusable skills

A skill is a reusable package of instructions, criteria, resources, and checks that teaches an AI how to execute a task consistently. It must declare sources, limits, inputs, outputs, and tests.

Expert route · Spec → Build → Verify

Research to skill

  1. 01

    Define the skill decision and user.

  2. 02

    Use Research Blueprint to scope questions, sources, and acceptance.

  3. 03

    Run Deep Research and retain report, sources, and date.

  4. 04

    Audit authority, coverage, tensions, rights, and gaps.

  5. 05

    Import only approved sources into the open notebook or your own.

  6. 06

    Configure the Notebook as a source-grounded advisor and inspect citations.

  7. 07

    Write the skill contract: trigger, inputs, outputs, limits, and no-go.

  8. 08

    Ask the AI to create the skill from research without copying private data.

  9. 09

    Optionally configure a community local NotebookLM MCP; sign in yourself, review permissions, and avoid sensitive information.

  10. 10

    Run positive and adversarial cases; fix until sources, outputs, and limits are verifiable.

Optional setup

Google offers Antigravity IDE for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Its official guide requires Chrome and a personal Gmail account. Install from the official source, use review-driven development, and confirm current plan limits.

AntigravityGoogle Codelab

NotebookLM MCP

NotebookLM MCP is a community integration, not an official Google connector. It may automate a browser and retain a local session. Review the repository, pin a version, sign in personally, and avoid confidential sources.
